answer_raw:
**Medellín** is your best bet for stretching a $4,000 monthly budget, as it is roughly 40–50% cheaper than Lisbon [2].

| City | Rent (1BR) | Total Monthly Budget |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Medellín** | **$700–$900** (Laureles, as of 2026-03-28) | **$1,300–$2,250** (as of 2026-03-28) |
| **Florianópolis** | **R$2,500–R$3,800** (as of 2026) | **R$6,365** (as of 2026-11-02) |
| **Lisbon** | **$1,400–$2,000** (as of 2026-03-28) | **$2,200–$3,200** (as of 2026-03-28) |

**Medellín** offers the most significant savings, with rent being about half the price of Lisbon and the overall cost of living being 40–50% lower [2]. A comfortable lifestyle there costs between **$1,300 and $2,250** per month [2].

In **Florianópolis**, a monthly budget for one person is estimated at **R$6,365** including rent and utilities as of 2026-11-02; if you exclude housing, the cost is roughly **R$3,472** as of 2026-11-s02. Rent for a 1-BR in a good area ranges from **R$2,500 to R$3,800** as of 2026 [3].

**Lisbon** is the most expensive of the three, costing roughly 60–80% more than Medellín [2]. A central 1-BR currently runs between **$1,400 and $2,000** (€1,300–€1,800) as of 2026-03-28, and a comfortable lifestyle there ranges from **$2,200 to $3,200** [2].
